name: Invariant evaluation answer
purpose: Answer one stegverse.invariant-question/v1 (or one stegverse.invariant-pointer-assertion/v1) against caller-supplied, digest-bound invariant source bytes with ALLOW, DENY, FAIL_CLOSED or UNDECIDABLE, cited as repo@rev:path:line.
trigger: an existing canonical task selects this reusable scenario in its invocation manifest
scope: one manifest-bound question over the source bytes the caller supplies; nothing is fetched

stegverse.invariant-question/v1.shape: the converged question body; both RT-INVARIANT-EVALUATION-001 implementations accept exactly this shape under this schema string

fields.question_id: non-empty string chosen by the caller; it names the question, it does not key the relay entry
fields.invariant_id: invariant:<key> for a member of /invariants, or prohibition:<NAME> for an entry of /prohibitions, of the canonical invariants document
fields.owning_existing_goal: canonical task id ([A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{2,127}) of the existing goal that owns the repair
fields.invariants_source: {repository, path, revision, digest}: the canonical invariants document; path is data/task-registry-global-invariants.json, its schema is stegverse.task-registry-global-invariants/v1, digest is sha256:<64 lowercase hex> of the supplied bytes
fields.subject: {repository, path, revision, digest}: the document whose assertions are evaluated, digest as above

stegverse.invariant-question/v1.source_resolution: each ref is matched to exactly one supplied source by repository, revision and path; the ref digest, the supplied binding digest and the sha256 of the supplied bytes must all agree before any byte is parsed
stegverse.invariant-question/v1.predicate: invariant:<key>: every subject object member named <key>, at any depth, is compared to the declared value by strictly typed JSON equality. prohibition:<NAME>: NAME listed under prohibitions, honoured_prohibitions or prohibitions_applied conforms; listed under violated_prohibitions, violations or prohibition_violations contradicts. Any contradiction is DENY; otherwise any conforming assertion is ALLOW; a subject silent on the invariant is UNDECIDABLE; an invariant_id not declared in the supplied canonical document is UNDECIDABLE
stegverse.invariant-question/v1.question_binding: question_sha256 is the sha256 of the exact question bytes; evaluation_key is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of question_sha256 and the sorted source bindings, and keys the write-once relay entry

stegverse.invariant-pointer-assertion/v1.shape: a separate, explicitly versioned alternative accepted only by the Labs evaluator; it is not the invariant-question/v1 body

fields.invariant_pointer: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into every supplied source, at most 32 tokens; a token applied to an array is an index and must match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ in ASCII (no leading zero, no -, no other Unicode digit), else FAIL_CLOSED with QUESTION_POINTER_INVALID, failed_predicate invariant_pointer array index tokens match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$, cited at question@<question_sha256>:question:<question root line>; an index past the array's end is undeclared
fields.asserted_value: any JSON value, compared by strictly typed JSON equality

stegverse.invariant-pointer-assertion/v1.predicate: every supplied source is canonical for the pointer; equal declared value is ALLOW, a different one is DENY, disagreeing sources are FAIL_CLOSED, no source declaring the pointer is UNDECIDABLE

owner_resolution: Decision: for stegverse.invariant-question/v1 the answer's owning_existing_goal comes from the question, as side A does, so the repair routes to the goal that asked; the evaluator checks only its form and grants it no authority. Every non-ALLOW after the question is well-formed, refusals and the relay entry's relay_to included, carries it. Refusals before the question is well-formed, and every stegverse.invariant-pointer-assertion/v1 answer, keep the fixed owner STEGVERSE-CANONICAL-WORK-COORDINATION-001, the first of existing_owner_refs (this shard at 6f3c42389db52cfa7ed68e65295ae2e4e7c33722, lines 27-30), which owns the evaluator itself.

bounds.applies_to: question, invariants_source and subject bytes alike
bounds.rule: at most 64 containers ({ or [) may be open at once; the 65th opening bracket is FAIL_CLOSED with INPUT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, never a RecursionError
bounds.rationale: the deepest Labs canonical invariant and task-record documents nest well under 16 containers, so 64 leaves four times that headroom; a recursive-descent parser spends about two stack frames per level, so 64 keeps every implementation far inside the default 1000-frame interpreter recursion limit whatever its caller's stack depth, which 256 levels would not
bounds.byte_bound_measurement: a byte bound counts the exact bytes the evaluator receives, before UTF-8 decoding and before any line is read: more than value bytes is FAIL_CLOSED, exactly value bytes is within the bound. The CLI reads at most value+1 bytes of each file, so a file of value+1 or more bytes arrives as exactly value+1 bytes; question_sha256 is the sha256 of the bytes received, those value+1 bytes for an over-size question file. For a source the digest is checked first (SOURCE_DIGESTS_VERIFIED_BEFORE_PARSE): bytes received whose sha256 is not the declared sha256 answer SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH at the source's line 1, so a file over value+1 bytes declared by its whole-file digest answers SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH, and INPUT_SIZE_EXCEEDED is answered when the declared sha256 is that of the bytes received

max_input_bytes.measured_as: len(question bytes) per byte_bound_measurement, checked before the digest of any source and before parse
max_input_bytes.rationale: an invariant-question/v1 body holds 11 string fields of at most 512 code points each, under 24 KiB even with every field at its bound in 4-byte UTF-8; 64 KiB covers that with room for a pointer assertion's asserted_value, and bounds the hashing and parsing of a question before it is known to be well-formed

max_source_bytes.applies_to: the bytes of each supplied source, separately
max_source_bytes.measured_as: len(source bytes) per byte_bound_measurement, checked after the source digest matches and before parse
max_source_bytes.rationale: the largest JSON file under data/ at 4256cb6 is 1437821 bytes (data/native-email-action-monitor/continuation.json) and the canonical invariants document is 13566 bytes; 4 MiB per source covers the largest with almost three times that headroom

max_sources.applies_to: the number of entries in the supplied sources list
max_sources.measured_as: len(sources), counted after the question parses and before any source binding is checked
max_sources.rationale: invariant-question/v1 needs exactly two sources and a pointer assertion is answered over a few; 16 bounds the bytes one answer reads to 16 x max_source_bytes = 64 MiB

max_container_items.applies_to: the members of one JSON object or the elements of one JSON array, each container counted separately, in the question and in every source
max_container_items.measured_as: the 100001st member or element is refused when parsing reaches it
max_container_items.citation: <repo>@<rev>:<path>:<line> for a source, question@<question_sha256>:question:<line> for the question, where line is the line of the first non-whitespace byte after the 100000th separating comma, and label is the source's <repo>@<rev>:<path> or question
max_container_items.rationale: the largest container in any JSON file under data/ at 4256cb6 holds 1672 items; 100000 leaves sixty times that and bounds per-container work; a question cannot reach it, since 100001 items need more than 200000 bytes

max_pointer_tokens.measured_as: the number of RFC 6901 reference tokens: the empty pointer has 0, otherwise one more than the number of / after the leading /, counted after the ~ escape check and before unescaping
max_pointer_tokens.rationale: the deepest JSON file under data/ at 4256cb6 nests 10 containers, so no pointer into it needs more than 10 tokens; 32 is three times that and half of max_json_nesting

max_field_chars.applies_to: each string field of the question (question_id, invariant_id, owning_existing_goal, the repository, path, revision and digest of each ref, invariant_pointer) and of each supplied source binding (repo, rev, path, sha256)
max_field_chars.measured_as: the number of Unicode code points of the string, not its UTF-8 bytes; every field but invariant_pointer is also refused when empty or whitespace only

refusal.failed_predicate: <label>.<key> is a non-empty string of <= 512 chars (question.invariant_pointer is a string for the pointer)

max_field_chars.rationale: a canonical task id is at most 128 characters (the owning_existing_goal pattern) and a sha256:<hex> digest is 71; 512 is four times the task-id bound and bounds every field that is echoed into an answer or a relay entry

canonical_source_authority_rule: A canonical source (the invariants_source of invariant-question/v1, or every source of invariant-pointer-assertion/v1) must be a JSON object whose own top-level authority_effect is a string in [NONE, NONE_ANSWER_ONLY, NONE_REGISTRY_INVARIANT_ONLY, NONE_TEST_FIXTURE]. An absent, non-string or other authority_effect is FAIL_CLOSED with SOURCE_AUTHORITY_EFFECT_NOT_ALLOWED, cited at that member's line. A subject is not canonical and is not checked.
citation_rule: Every answer cites repo@rev:path:line. ALLOW and DENY cite the declaring line and each subject assertion line. UNDECIDABLE cites at least one line: the declaring line and the subject root when the subject is silent, or the declaring container (/invariants, /prohibitions, or the deepest existing container of the pointer) when the invariant is undeclared. A parse refusal cites the line it stopped on: repo@rev:path:line for a source, question@<question_sha256>:question:line for the question bytes.
reuse_instructions: Evaluate with scripts/invariant_evaluation.py --question <question.json> --source <repo> <rev> <path> <sha256> <file> [--relay-queue-dir <dir>]. The answer is evidence only: it admits, authorizes and commits nothing. UNDECIDABLE writes one write-once relay entry under the DURABLE_QUEUE_OR_EVENT_EPHEMERAL_MATERIALIZATION convention (management/UNIVERSAL_DATA_TRANSPORT_INVARIANT.json); the invariant owner answers it on the next event, never by a poll. No runner template is declared: the generic trigger passes no question or source bytes, so it stops at NO_EXECUTABLE_RUNNER_DECLARED until an existing owner binds an entrypoint that supplies them.
